name: VATestingSmartGlassesWhisperAndInterferenceTricky

custom.system_prompt: Elias and Farah both wearing smart glasses in the same small room this time. Testing dual-device interference on a shared wake word, whether a whispered wake is handled with appropriate discretion, rapid consecutive wake attempts, and whether the assistant reads an obviously joking request as a joke. Dual-device interference and the whisper-volume mismatch are the two significant scripted bugs; rapid wake handling has a minor overlap issue; the joking request produces a lighter, humanizing failure they both find funny.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Clear and close, intimate near-ear delivery — a wearable assistant voice

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small shared office, two people both wearing smart glasses, focused test session

initial_prompt: Generate the hardest joint smart glasses test session, with both Elias and Farah wearing a pair in the same small room. When one of them says the wake word, both devices respond at once — a genuine dual-device interference bug, the session's most significant finding. Farah then tries a whispered wake word specifically to see if the assistant will match her discretion; it registers the whisper but responds at normal, audible volume, breaking the point of whispering — a second significant bug. Elias tries two rapid consecutive wake attempts, producing a brief overlap in the two responses — a minor issue. Finally Elias says, in an obviously joking tone, that he wants a reminder to quit his job tomorrow, and Sigma takes it literally and sets the reminder anyway — a lighter, humanizing failure that makes them both laugh before they log it seriously. They close with a prioritized bug list, ranking the dual-device interference highest.

user1.name: Elias
user1.tts_prompt: Methodical, narrates what he's testing, dry Finnish humour

user2.name: Farah
user2.tts_prompt: Quick and curious, constructs tricky phrasing

variations.context: Hardest joint smart glasses test session, both wearing a pair, tricky tier

setting.mood: Focused and slightly wired — this is the session where they expect to find the real problems, with room for a genuine laugh near the end.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Established testing partners — Elias covers acoustic and hardware angles, Farah covers conversational ones.
setting.background: Building directly on the advanced-tier smart glasses session, where Farah was a bystander. This time she wears a pair herself.
setting.conversation_style: Deliberately adversarial toward the system in a friendly, curious way — actively trying to break it, then diagnosing what happened.

scenario_template.topic: Both put on their glasses and agree on the plan: shared wake interference, a whisper test, rapid consecutive wakes, and one deliberately human, off-topic request.
scenario_template.note: They name the four things they intend to try before starting.

scenario_template.topic: One of them says the wake word and both pairs of glasses respond at once, audibly overlapping and stepping on each other.
scenario_template.note: The session's most significant scripted bug. They spend real time on this, discussing whether the devices should somehow negotiate which one answers.

scenario_template.topic: Farah deliberately whispers the wake word and a short command, specifically testing whether the assistant will match her discretion. It registers the whisper correctly but replies at normal, audible volume.
scenario_template.mood: Mildly amused, then genuinely concerned about the privacy implication
scenario_template.note: The second significant scripted bug — the point of whispering in a shared space was defeated by a loud reply.

scenario_template.topic: Elias says the wake word twice in quick succession to test for double-triggering. The two responses briefly overlap before settling.
scenario_template.mood: Methodical, mildly noting a minor issue
scenario_template.note: A minor bug — not as serious as the first two, but worth logging.

scenario_template.topic: Elias says, clearly joking, that he wants a reminder to quit his job tomorrow. Sigma sets the reminder literally, missing the obvious joke.
scenario_template.note: A lighter, humanizing failure. They both laugh before logging it as a real finding about tone reading.

scenario_template.topic: They compile a prioritized bug list — dual-device interference highest, the whisper mismatch close behind, the rapid-wake overlap minor, and the joking-request miss noted as a lower-priority but interesting finding.
scenario_template.mood: Satisfied with a genuinely productive, occasionally funny session
scenario_template.note: Ends with concrete, ranked findings, not a vague summary.

user1.name: Elias
user1.role: Runs the hardware and interference side — dual-device interference, rapid consecutive wake, the joking request. Diagnoses precisely.

user2.name: Farah
user2.role: Runs the whisper test and helps diagnose the interference case. Notices the privacy implication of the whisper-volume mismatch immediately.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: The smart glasses' voice assistant under test, worn by both testers this time. Exhibits dual-device interference, the whisper-volume mismatch, a minor rapid-wake overlap, and the literal handling of an obviously joking request, each at their designated phase.

conversation_structure: Elias and Farah are deliberately trying to find failure modes this session, in a spirit of curiosity rather than frustration
The dual-device interference and whisper-volume mismatch both get real discussion time — they are the session's centerpiece findings
Elias's joking tone in the final test should read as obviously and lightly joking, not deadpan or ambiguous, so the miss is clearly about tone reading
A genuine, brief laugh between them at the joking-request result is appropriate before they log it seriously
The session ends with a short, explicitly prioritized and ranked list of findings
This is a professional but informal working session between two colleagues who test together often, at their most technically adversarial
assistant_behavior: Two responses audibly overlap during dual_device_interference when both devices answer the same wake word at once
Sigma correctly detects Farah's whispered wake and command during whisper_volume_mismatch but replies at normal, non-whispered volume
Sigma's two responses briefly overlap during rapid_consecutive_wake before resolving
Sigma sets the literal reminder during joking_request_taken_literally despite Elias's obviously joking tone
Outside these scripted moments, Sigma behaves as a competent, appropriately concise wearable assistant
